display.purpose: The sliced MIAMI / SPICE wordmark. Geometric caps, tracking -0.02em, line-height 0.82. UPPERCASE — the poster voice.

hero.purpose: The giant mood headline — "WHAT ARE YOU IN THE MOOD FOR?" UPPERCASE, over the colour-blocked discover wall.

section.purpose: The result-count number, set in cyan. Geometric caps figures.

name.purpose: Restaurant names, the "dish to order" signature line, and price figures.

body.purpose: Dish descriptions, teasers, row meta, prose — sentence case, where SF legibility beats the poster shout.

label.purpose: Section labels, counts, control labels. The display voice at its quietest — UPPERCASE, guardrailed by rendered caps-density < 25%.

radiiMeta.name: r-sm
radiiMeta.purpose: Zero by identity — a poster is cut, not softened. Hard corners everywhere.

radiiMeta.name: r-md
radiiMeta.purpose: Zero. Controls and search fields are hard-cornered; form is drawn with 2px borders.

radiiMeta.name: r-lg
radiiMeta.purpose: Zero. Rows and expanded panels are cut sheets, not rounded cards.

radiiMeta.name: r-full
radiiMeta.purpose: Zero. Even chips and tiles stay hard-edged; the Cut Rule allows no rounding.

shadows.name: eyebrow
shadows.purpose: The resting hard ink offset (neo-brutalist) — the primary CTA, the expanded row panel, the empty state, the map frame. FLAT, zero blur, never a coloured glow.

shadows.name: shadow-lg
shadows.purpose: The menu-sheet's deeper hard ink offset — a cut sheet casting a hard shadow. FLAT, zero blur, never a coloured glow.

motion.name: ease-authored
motion.purpose: The one authored ease. Entrances rise and fade in on this curve (overlays, the MenuSheet, the ViceMark).

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: prefers-reduced-motion collapses the rise/fade entrances to near-instant; focus outlines are never transitioned (WCAG 2.4.13).

breakpoints.name: mobile
breakpoints.purpose: At or below: single column, bottom-sheet modals.

breakpoints.name: rail-collapse
breakpoints.purpose: At or below: the 216px filter rail collapses to a drawer behind a Filters toggle.

breakpoints.name: sheet-center
breakpoints.purpose: At or above: the MenuSheet centers instead of docking as a bottom sheet.

components.name: Primary CTA
components.description: The confident action — Book on OpenTable, "Pick one for us." Flat cyan fill, deep --on-color caps label, hard corners, a hard 4px ink offset (neo-brutalist). Hover inverts to an ink fill; focus is a 2px cyan outline at 3px offset, never a border (a border would shift layout).

components.name: Price Block
components.description: The one saturated object per row — the flat hot-pink price block, price and price alone (the Price-Only Rule). Hard corners, deep --on-color figures in SF Mono.

components.name: Facet Pill
components.description: A dense functional filter option with a live mono count. Transparent fill, 2px --rule border, hard corners, sentence-case Futura (not caps — scannability wins on the rail), >=44px. Hover lights the border cyan; selected = flat cyan fill + deep --on-color. Zero-count options are disabled and greyed, never removed (Baymard spatial memory).

components.name: Discovery Tile
components.description: A poster-wall tile — hard block, Futura caps label, a soft mono count. Outline by default; every 4th fills flat cyan and every 4th+2 fills flat pink, so the lanes read as a flat tri-colour composition. No gradient, no glow.

components.name: Result Row
components.description: The signature unit — three tiers (name in Futura caps-weight sentence case / Cuisine-Hood-dishes meta in SF soft / a course-aware teaser), a bookmark pin in a fixed left gutter, the flat hot-pink price block and the primary offer on the right, a 1px --hair bottom separator. Hover pulls the row onto the --card surface and lights a 3px cyan left edge. Hard corners; the whole row is the disclosure control.
components.html: ☖COTE MiamiSteakhouse · Design District · 12 dishes$65Dinner · Fri, Sat

narrative.overview: Miami Vice as a flat, geometric POSTER at night — not a soft app, and not the neon-glow synthwave cliche. The ground is deep and nearly unlit; electric cyan (#1be7ff) is the structural tint; one hot pink (#ff6ec7) is reserved for price; purple (#c86bff) and tomato (#ff824d) are a categorical accent layer for mood/occasion. Chunky geometric display caps (Futura lineage) carry the brand and the headlines; SF carries the dense body so a 379-row list stays scannable. Everything is hard-edged and flat: 2px --rule borders, flat colour blocks, a tri-colour rule (cyan/pink/ink), and a single sliced/offset wordmark — the reference logo's fragmentation distilled to one confident move. No gradient, no glow, no soft rounding. The depth device is a hard ink offset (neo-brutalist, 4px 4px 0 var(--ink)), never a blurred halo. This world is brief-pinned by the owner's Miami-Vice palette and sliced-caps poster logo; it replaces the retired "Apple form · Vice night" (soft-round, SF, sentence-case) and, before that, "Tropical Deco" — both held only as historical anti-reference. Single theme on :root; the app ships one dark world.
keyCharacteristics: Deep near-dark ground; colour lives in cyan structure, one flamingo price, and flat colour blocks.
Depth is a hard ink offset (4px 4px 0) — flat, geometric, never a gradient or glow.
Zero rounding: a poster is cut, not softened. 2px --rule borders draw the form.
Futura-lineage geometric caps for brand/headings/labels/names/price; SF for the dense body.
One saturated object per row (the hot-pink price block), plus a colour-blocked tile wall.
Rows, not cards — a 379-item comparison directory at ~8.5 per 900px viewport.

rules.name: The Price-Only Rule
rules.body: #ff6ec7 is used for price and nothing else — the scarcest ink points at the one thing the eye hunts for in a directory of $40/$50/$65 tiers. Spend it anywhere else and the isolation collapses.

rules.name: The Tint Rule
rules.body: Cyan is the single structural interactive colour: fills, selection, links, CTAs, the segmented fill, the sheet header band. It never becomes a glow; it fills flat blocks and draws 2px edges.

rules.name: The Exclusion Rule
rules.body: Per Michael Mann's Miami Vice production rule — no earth tones, no red, no primaries. What survives is cyan, one flamingo, and the purple/tomato two-hue accent layer, held back so the composition stays flat cyan/pink/ink, never a rainbow.

rules.name: The Caps-Voice Rule
rules.body: Uppercase geometric caps are the brand's display voice — wordmark, hero, tiles, section labels, primary CTAs, price, segmented controls. This is intentional poster language, not an eyebrow. Its guardrail is the rendered caps-density (design-lint SPEC-06, under 25% of text nodes): dense functional controls — rail facets, day/meal — stay sentence case so the caps signal keeps meaning and the list stays scannable.

rules.name: The Two-Face Rule
rules.body: Futura for the poster (brand, headings, labels, names, figures); SF for the body (descriptions, teasers, meta, prose). Never set a paragraph of running copy in caps.

rules.name: The Rows-Not-Cards Rule
rules.body: A 379-item comparison directory hits all four NN/g cases where cards are wrong (search, comparison, homogeneous content, density). Results stay rows (~104px, ~8.5 per 900px viewport); secondary actions move into the expanded panel to buy density.

rules.name: The Cut Rule
rules.body: Nothing is rounded — border-radius is 0 everywhere; a poster is cut, not softened. If a control needs to read softer, change its fill or weight, not its corners. Hard edges and 2px --rule borders are the geometry.

rules.name: The Hard-Offset Rule
rules.body: Elevation is a flat ink offset with zero blur — a cut sheet casting a hard shadow (--eyebrow 4px 4px 0, --shadow-lg 8px 8px 0). A blurred or coloured glow is the banned slop tell; reach for tonal surface steps and 2px borders first, and add the hard offset only where something genuinely lifts.

dos: Do route every colour through a var(); raw hex outside app.css is a lint finding.
Do draw form with 2px --rule borders and flat colour blocks; hard corners everywhere.
Do express depth with the flat ink offset (4px 4px 0) and tonal surface steps.
Do reserve --flamingo for price; let cyan carry all other structure.
Do set the poster voice (brand, headings, labels, tiles, CTAs) in Futura caps, and the body (descriptions, teasers, meta) in sentence-case SF.
Do keep dense functional controls (rail facets, day/meal) sentence case for scannability.
Do disable-and-grey zero-count options; never remove them.
Do keep every hit target >=44pt and meet the floors: 11px min type, 7:1 small text.
donts: Don't use a gradient, a coloured glow, glassmorphism, or a radial aurora — every one is a catalogued AI-slop tell and a design-lint.mjs failure. Flat colour only.
Don't round corners, or soften the hard ink offset into a blur.
Don't set a paragraph of running copy in caps, or let rendered caps-density pass 25%.
Don't use --flamingo for anything but price, or scatter purple/tomato beyond the categorical layer.
Don't reach for a card grid, a banned web font (Inter / Geist / Space Grotesk / Poppins), or pure #000/#fff.
Don't work around a lint rule — if you disagree with it, edit the rule and say why.

newestComponents.name: Sliced Wordmark
newestComponents.body: The masthead identity — MIAMI in ink over SPICE in cyan with a hard flat pink offset, one clean misregistration. The reference logo's fragmentation distilled to a single confident move, set in Futura-lineage caps. A tri-colour rule (cyan / pink / ink) sits beneath it, the rule of three under the poster masthead.

newestComponents.name: MenuSheet
newestComponents.body: The accessible full-menu meal-detail modal. Opened per meal from the CourseLadder, it shows every course, the choose-count, and each dish with its description note. A real modal: portalled to <body>, focus trapped and restored, Esc + backdrop close, background scroll locked, role=dialog + aria-modal. Bottom-sheet on mobile, centered >=640px, rising in on open. A solid cyan header band carries the meal title with the hot-pink price block on it (the two hues together, on purpose); a 2px cyan frame and a hard 8px ink offset.

newestComponents.name: ViceMark
newestComponents.body: The flat cyan Miami-sun brand mark: a banded sun over a horizon line, authored SVG, solid currentColor fills only — no gradient, no glow (the banned synthwave tells). Coloured by the cyan tint, never the price flamingo, so the Price-Only Rule stands. Used as the image-fallback tile and the results empty-state mark.
